title: I'm tired of skinny functional nerds (@MovementbyDavid)
summary: Critique of functional-fitness creator MovementbyDavid's 'skinny but strong' claim. NH credits functional training as an accessible beginner entry point but argues all training is functional, that the feats shown are weak, and that generalist channels give poor strength and hypertrophy advice while using aesthetic thumbnails and disparaging bodybuilding.
claims: Functional/bodyweight training is the ultimate entry routine for beginners: no gym or equipment needed, not intimidating, and no rep ranges, RIR or plate math to learn
Plate math is a gatekeeper for novices in the gym
Functional fitness has succeeded in getting mainstream people moving who just want health benefits
Life-or-death justifications like hanging from a bridge are silly; pull-ups are worth doing because they are fun and build strength
An exercise's value is the attributes it builds (e.g. bear crawl trains core, upper back, shoulders), not the movement itself; by that logic every resistance exercise is functional
Bodybuilding trains muscles directly through their function (a curl trains elbow flexion and supination), with aesthetics as a secondary outcome
A 140 lb lifter doing a few push-ups, pistols, pull-ups, a 60 lb overhead press and two handstand push-ups is weak; most should do that after a year of training
The lighter you are, the easier calisthenics movements become
Lifters at ~140 lb can squat 400 lb, bench 250 lb and overhead press bodyweight for reps
Being stronger than the untrained average is not being strong; fitness should raise standards, not lower them
Training without a specific goal is like getting good at hammering nails without building a house; eventually you must specialize to progress and stay engaged
Anything done in the gym is functional as long as it aligns with your goal
Flexibility, like toe-touching, mostly exists for its own sake unless your sport or job needs it; heavy deadlifts gave him bigger hamstrings and glutes
Stay in your lane: specialists become good at their area and bad at the rest, so take advice from people who have that quality
Abs are built by training them hard in the gym (weighted sit-ups, windshield wipers), not just by dieting
Functional channels borrow aesthetic thumbnails while disparaging bodybuilding, repeating what powerlifting YouTube did ~10 years ago
Many skinny teens assume everyone big is on PEDs and settle for functional training, staying in their comfort zone; anyone can get big naturally with proper bodybuilding training
All training purposes are 'vain' because they all serve self-improvement; pursue what actually satisfies you or you will end up bitter
If aesthetics got you into fitness, seek specialist teachers in that, not generalists
exercises: fun, overall strength; not more 'functional' than other lifts
trains core, upper back and shoulders
bigger hamstrings and glutes than flexibility work
